To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the balance of protein and energy in the diet may be a critical factor determining the long-term health of the fetus and offspring.
the low protein S9 maternal diet protocol is more effective in programming hypertension in the offspring than the H9 diet protocol.
the balance of protein and carbohydrate in the diet is a critical determinant of programming effects of maternal under nutrition on blood pressure in the offspring.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of maternal nutrition on the development of the cardiovascular system in the offspring.
the effects of maternal undernourishment in pregnancy on the development of the cardiovascular system in the offspring.
the long-term effects of early nutritional insult upon the developing cardiovascular system, and the mechanisms that may underlie this relationship.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the balance of protein and energy, and the balance of protein, fat and carbohydrate, are critical determinants of the effects of maternal under-nutrition in pregnancy on fetal growth and development.
the balance of protein and fat, and the type of carbohydrate, are important factors in the programming of cardiovascular disease.
maternal protein restriction during pregnancy is associated with a reduction in fetal growth and a subsequent elevation in blood pressure in the offspring.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the S18 diet was the most beneficial for the mother, and the S9 diet was the most detrimental for the offspring, in terms of both maternal weight gain and offspring blood pressure.

the low protein diet protocol that was used to program hypertension was the one that had the lowest methionine content, the highest fat content, the lowest carbohydrate content and the lowest polyunsaturated to saturated ratio of fatty acids.
a high fat diet, with a relatively high content of polyunsaturated fatty acids, is protective in terms of programming of the cardiovascular system in utero.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the balance of protein and carbohydrate in the diet is a key determinant of the long term health consequences of low protein feeding in pregnancy.
different low protein diets can have different programming effects on offspring blood pressure.
the composition of a low protein (LP) diet is critical in determining its effects on fetal growth and programming of hypertension in rat pregnancy.
